sections.h2: How is Ogle County laid out?
sections.html:
Ogle County spreads across northern Illinois below Rockford. Oregon holds the courthouse, while Rochelle is the county's most populous city. It was formed in 1836 from Jo Daviess and LaSalle counties and named for Captain Joseph Ogle; Lee County was carved from its southern part in 1839. Land area is about 759 square miles, and it adjoins Winnebago, Boone, DeKalb, Lee, Whiteside, Carroll and Stephenson counties.

Freight rail is part of the landscape: Union Pacific, BNSF and Canadian Pacific Kansas City lines all pass through. Farming, chiefly corn and soybeans, sits beside manufacturing as a major activity. Schools come from districts such as Oregon, Byron, Polo, Ashton, Forrestville Valley, Meridian, Eastland and Hiawatha, plus the Rochelle Township High School district.

sections.h2: What does the Ogle County Treasurer handle, and what does everyone else do?
sections.html:
Collection of real estate and mobile home tax belongs to the Treasurer, who then distributes it to each taxing body. Visit the old Courthouse, 105 S. 5th Street, Oregon, weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30, closed on holidays. By mail, use Ogle County Collector, P.O. Box 40, Oregon, IL 61061.

Valuation sits with the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 732-1150. That office's explainer says roughly 60 percent of a bill funds the local school district, with the rest shared by the county, municipalities, parks, libraries, fire districts, townships and special districts. Springfield writes the rules yet takes none of the money.

sections.h2: Which dates applied to the 2025 bills in Ogle County?
sections.html:
Mailing took place May 1, 2026, and one document carried stubs for both installments; the Treasurer cautioned that nothing else would arrive ahead of the second. Every date below is past, and each year brings a fresh set.

  • Mobile home tax: May 15, 2026.
  • First installment: Monday, June 8, 2026.
  • Second installment: Tuesday, September 8, 2026.
  • Certified funds only, with no online payments: October 1, 2026.
  • Last day to pay: Wednesday, November 4, 2026.
  • Tax sale of real estate and mobile homes: Thursday, November 5, 2026.

The county charges 1.5% for every month a payment runs late, and a partial month is billed as a whole one. Mail postmarked by the due date stays on time under state law, which marks first-installment delinquency at the later of June 1 or the day following the printed date (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

sections.h2: How can you pay or search a bill in Ogle County?
sections.html:
Accepted forms are cash, a check payable to Ogle County Collector, or a credit card, either at the Treasurer's desk or at any bank in Ogle County. An online option exists too; it adds a fee the page asks you to review first, and a confirmation worth keeping.

The county's lookup works from an address or a 10-digit parcel number. Enter just the house number and street name, skipping N or S and endings like Ave. The public cannot see owner names. A prepayment program takes deposits between December 1 and April 1 using a form from the Treasurer's website.

Ahead of a sale, run the parcel in the lookup and ask the office whether any earlier year is still open.

sections.h2: How does Ogle County assess a home?
sections.html:
Farmland aside, the target is one third of market value, applied evenly across a jurisdiction. An elected township assessor places the first values on property inside the township, and the Supervisor of Assessments oversees that work for the county.

The Supervisor's explainer contrasts property tax with income and sales tax: it rests on real estate value and holds steadier through economic swings, which makes it a dependable base for local agencies.

sections.h2: How does an assessment appeal work in Ogle County?
sections.html:
A three-person Board of Review, appointed by the County Board under 35 ILCS 200/16-20, takes the case. Its seats split two to one between the parties. The filing window is generally 30 days after your township's assessment list appears, matching the current-year rule in 35 ILCS 200/16-55.

  • Send by U.S. Mail with a postmark on or before the last day, or hand it in by then.
  • Faxes, emails and other electronic filings are refused.
  • Read the Board's rules and the form's instructions beforehand. Commercial property has its own form, and a Request to Intervene form is available.

The Board weighs what the owner and the township assessor submit and may set a hearing. Meetings pick up in November, December and January once deadlines pass, and the same Board decides exemption requests.

sections.h2: How much homestead relief can an Ogle County owner expect?
sections.html:
State law caps the general homestead reduction at $6,000 of equalized value for counties such as Ogle that do not touch a 3,000,000-resident county (35 ILCS 200/15-175). Requests for other exemptions go to the Board of Review.

Illinois also has senior and veteran programs. Call the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 732-1150 to learn which applications fit your household.

sections.h2: What does an Ogle County seller need to settle with the tax office?
sections.html:
Pull the parcel in the online lookup, then ask the Treasurer for the payoff on whatever installment is open. At closing the title company prorates the year, and the settlement statement lists each side's share.

Balances still unpaid after the final payment day go to the tax sale. Following a sale, the owner of a one-to-six unit residence has at least 2 1/2 years to redeem, other property at least 2 years, and a tax buyer may stretch either to 3 years (35 ILCS 200/21-350, as summarized by the DuPage County Clerk).

faqs.q: What was the final payment day before the 2026 Ogle County sale?
faqs.a: It was November 4, 2026, one day ahead of the November 5 sale. From October 1 only certified funds were taken and online payments ended.

faqs.q: Does Ogle County mail a separate second installment bill?
faqs.a: No. One bill with two stubs is mailed, and the Treasurer says nothing more comes before the second installment, so keep it.

faqs.q: How do I find my Ogle County parcel number?
faqs.a: Look on the tax bill for a 10-digit number, usually formatted XX-XX-XXX-XXX. The online lookup can also find it from a house number and street name.

faqs.q: Can I file an Ogle County assessment appeal by email?
faqs.a: No. The Board takes appeals only by postmarked U.S. Mail or hand delivery by the deadline, and it does not accept fax or electronic filings.

faqs.q: Who owes the late fee on an Ogle County bill?
faqs.a: The property owner does. The fee is 1.5% per month, a fraction of a month counts as a full one, and a mailed payment avoids it only when postmarked by the due date.
